## Purpose
Builds the co-flowering synchrony metric (circular / von Mises overlap) and
writes the transect-year synchrony files used by `02_` and `03_`.



### Load data
```{r load pheno data}
#make sure working dir is folder that also has data/ directory
# SEV Phenology data
phen <- read.csv("data/sev137_plant_phenology.2023.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) 
# List of animal-pollinated plants compiled by E. Martin
bee_poll_list <- read.csv("data/animal_poll_floral_async.csv") %>%
  dplyr::rename(species = kartez)
```

## Calculating synchrony (co-flowering overlap)
We used co-flowering overlap as a metric of floral synchrony. This method uses circular statistics to generate overlap values for all species pairs. This calculation is computationally intensive, so it is possible to skip to Analysis 1 and load in the resulting csv directly.

Wrangle phenology data and subset to animal-pollinated species 
```{r phen data wrangling}
# Ensure columns exist
required_cols <- c("date", "site", "web", "species", "reproduction")
stopifnot(all(required_cols %in% colnames(phen)))

# Remove NA months and unwanted sites
phen <- phen %>%
  filter(!is.na(date), site == "B"|site == "C"|site == "G") %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(substr(date, 1, 4)),
    month = as.integer(substr(date, 6, 7)),
    day = as.integer(substr(date, 9, 10))
  )

length(unique(phen$species))
#293 total plant species in the phenology dataset

#Keep only plant species that are animal-pollinated 
phen_bee <- phen %>% semi_join(bee_poll_list, by = "species")

# Keep only records with flowering reproduction codes (exclude "Z", "B", "FR")
# This gives us a data-set with abundance of plants that ARE IN FLOWER for each month
phen_flo <- phen_bee %>%
  filter(!reproduction %in% c("Z", "B", "FR"))

# Summarize flowering counts by species/site/year/month/web

# Detach plyr to avoid conflicts with dplyr
if ("package:plyr" %in% search()) detach("package:plyr", unload = TRUE)

# There are 5 webs at each site, which are surveyed each month within each year.
# This function summarizes the number of flowering individuals of a species in each web/site/month/year.
#notably, since we are excluding reproduction codes we are only calculating overlap for 
# species that ARE IN FLOWER. if not in flower, not in dataset, minmum flospec_count value is 1
phen_flower <- phen_flo %>%
  group_by(year, month, site, web, species) %>%
  summarise(flospec_count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Pivot wider 
wide_flower <- phen_flower %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = species,
    values_from = flospec_count,
    values_fill = 0
  )

# Convert back to long format if needed
phen_flower_long <- wide_flower %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(year, month, site, web),
    names_to = "species",
    values_to = "flospec_count"
  )

length(unique(phen_flower_long$species))
#142 animal pollinated plant species

#calculate bloom richness at each web (transect)
rich_ty <- phen_flower_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(flospec_count > 0) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(year, site, web, species) %>%
  dplyr::count(year, site, web, name = "n_species")
summary(rich_ty)
#mean transect x site x year richness is 20.9, median is 21.
#notably, when we exclude species based on them having to flower in at least 2 or 3 months of EACH year, we go down to about a #bloom richness of 4. The majority of our species are transient (short time window) blooming

write.csv(rich_ty, "data/richness_by_transectyear.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

Generate daily-resolution distributions
```{r von mises kernal density}
# Helper to compute circular kernel density estimate (von Mises)
densityFit <- function(x_rad, grid_rad, bandwidth) {
  # ensure input is numeric radians in [0, 2π]
  n <- length(x_rad)
  if (n == 0) return(rep(0, length(grid_rad)))
  
  # von Mises kernel density estimation manually
  res <- sapply(grid_rad, function(theta) {
    sum(exp(bandwidth * cos(theta - x_rad))) / (2 * pi * besselI(bandwidth, 0))
  })
  return(res)  # raw von Mises density; normalized to unit area in pheno.imputation
}

pheno.imputation <- function(rownum, ref_list, dat) {
  a <- ref_list[rownum, ]
  
  # Filter for the species/year/site/WEB combination
  sub <- dat %>%
    filter(species == a$species,
           year == a$year,
           site == a$site,
           web == a$web)
  
  # Skip if empty
  if (nrow(sub) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  # Skip if missing or all zero flowering counts
  if (all(is.na(sub$flospec_count)) || max(sub$flospec_count, na.rm = TRUE) == 0)
    return(NULL)
  
  # Map month to approximate DOY
  month_to_doy <- c(`3`=80, `4`=110, `5`=140, `6`=170, `7`=200,
                    `8`=230, `9`=260, `10`=290)
  sub <- sub %>%
    mutate(DOY = month_to_doy[as.character(month)]) %>%
    filter(!is.na(DOY))
  
  if (nrow(sub) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  # Count-shaped sample: repeat each month's DOY by its flowering count so the
  # kernel density reflects the WITHIN-species relative flowering intensity
  # across months. The density is normalized to unit area below, so between-
  # species magnitude (and the 10-individual censoring ceiling) drops out and
  # the overlap is the coefficient of overlapping (Ridout & Linkie 2009).
  lf <- rep(sub$DOY, times = sub$flospec_count)
  if (length(lf) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  # Convert to radians for circular KDE
  lf_rad <- (lf / 365) * 2 * pi
  day_rad <- (1:365 / 365) * 2 * pi
  
  # Compute von Mises kernel
  band <- vm.kde(lf_rad, thumb = "tay", rads = TRUE)$h
  if (is.nan(band) || is.null(band)) band <- 16.13
  
  circ_dist <- densityFit(lf_rad, day_rad, band)
  # Normalize to a unit-area probability density (Ridout & Linkie 2009) so that
  # overlap is the coefficient of overlapping, not an abundance-weighted metric
  circ_dist <- circ_dist / sum(circ_dist, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  data.frame(
    DOY = 1:365,
    abund = circ_dist,
    year = a$year,
    species = a$species,
    site = a$site,
    web = a$web,
    band = band
  )
}
```

Apply to all combinations
```{r apply to combos}
plant_list <- phen_flower_long %>%
  select(year, site, species, web) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  as.data.frame()

datalist <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(plant_list))) {
  tryCatch({
    dat_i <- pheno.imputation(i, plant_list, phen_flower_long)
    if (!is.null(dat_i)) {
      datalist[[length(datalist) + 1]] <- dat_i
    }
    if (i %% 100 == 0) cat("Processed", i, "of", nrow(plant_list), "combinations\n")
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Error at row ", i, ": ", e$message)
  })
}

# Combine
pheno_distributions <- data.table::rbindlist(datalist, fill = TRUE)
summary(pheno_distributions)
```

Generate species-species pairs per year/site/web
NOTE: 
 * There were 2 year-site-web groups in which only one species was present (and thus, co-flowering cannot be calculated) 
 * We used `phen_distrib_check %>% count(year, site, web, name = "n_species") %>% filter(n_species < 2)` to confirm the above
 * We removed these groups from the data set using `if (length(.x) < 2) return(NULL)`
 
```{r generate pairs}
phen_distrib_check <- pheno_distributions %>%
  select(year, site, web, species) %>%
  distinct()
summary(phen_distrib_check)

# Generate species-species pairs per year/site/web

plant_pairs <- phen_distrib_check %>%
  group_by(year, site, web) %>%
  summarise(species_list = list(species), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pairs = map(species_list, ~{
    if (length(.x) < 2) return(NULL) # ignores year/site/web grps with <2 species
    t(combn(.x, 2)) %>% as.data.frame() })) %>%
  select(-species_list) %>%
  unnest(pairs) %>%
  rename(species.x = V1, species.y = V2) %>%
  mutate(pair_id = pmap_chr(list(species.x, species.y),
        ~paste(sort(c(..1, ..2)), collapse = "_")),
         row = row_number()) %>%
  distinct(year, site, web, pair_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
plant_pairs %>%
  dplyr::count(site, web, year, name = "n_pairs") %>%   # pairs in each web × year
  dplyr::group_by(site) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_pairs = median(n_pairs),
    mean_pairs   = mean(n_pairs),
    min_pairs    = min(n_pairs),
    max_pairs    = max(n_pairs),
    n_webyears   = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# ======================================================================
# a species PAIR must co-flower in >= MIN_COFLOWER_YEARS distinct years to
# enter the overlap calculation. Counted per (site, pair_id) as the number
# of distinct years the pair co-occurs in >= 1 web 
# This drops pairs that rarely flower together and would
# otherwise deflate mean pairwise overlap -- i.e. it prevents the low-
# synchrony floor from being driven by species that never really co-flower
# rather than by genuine phenological divergence. Co-flower years are counted
# per (site, pair_id) across the 22 study years, at the SITE level (pooling a
# site's 5 webs); switch the grouping to c("site","web","pair_id") below for a
# stricter per-transect criterion.
# ======================================================================
MIN_COFLOWER_YEARS <- 7L

pair_coflower_years <- plant_pairs %>%
  dplyr::distinct(site, pair_id, year) %>%
  dplyr::count(site, pair_id, name = "n_coflower_years")

plant_pairs <- plant_pairs %>%
  dplyr::left_join(pair_coflower_years, by = c("site", "pair_id")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_coflower_years >= MIN_COFLOWER_YEARS)
plant_pairs %>%
  dplyr::count(site, web, year, name = "n_pairs") %>%   # pairs in each web × year
  dplyr::group_by(site) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_pairs = median(n_pairs),
    mean_pairs   = mean(n_pairs),
    min_pairs    = min(n_pairs),
    max_pairs    = max(n_pairs),
    n_webyears   = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
#years of data per site and web
plant_pairs %>% distinct(site, web, year) %>% count(site, web, name = "n_years") %>% print(n = Inf)
plant_pairs %>% distinct(site, year) %>% count(site, name = "n_years") %>% print(n = Inf)
```

Calculate interspecific overlap
```{r calculate overlap}
inter_synchrony <- function(rownum, ref_pairs, dat) {
  a <- ref_pairs[rownum, ]

  sub1 <- dat %>% filter(species == a$species.x, year == a$year, site == a$site, web == a$web)
  sub2 <- dat %>% filter(species == a$species.y, year == a$year, site == a$site, web == a$web)

  d <- data.frame(
    DOY = sub1$DOY,
    species1 = sub1$abund,
    species2 = sub2$abund
  )

  d$min <- pmin(d$species1, d$species2)

  # Coefficient of overlapping (Delta): the shared area of the two unit-area
  # flowering densities (Weitzman 1970; Ridout & Linkie 2009). Because each
  # density integrates to 1, Delta ranges 0 (no overlap) to 1 (identical).
  delta <- integrate.xy(d$DOY, d$min)

  data.frame(
    year = a$year,
    species.x = a$species.x,
    species.y = a$species.y,
    site = a$site,
    web = a$web,
    overlap = delta
  )
}

# Loop through all pairs
datalist_overlap <- list()

library(furrr)
library(data.table)
library(sfsmisc)   # for integrate.xy

plant_pairs_test <- plant_pairs %>%
  filter(year == 2010, site == "C", web == 2) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 10)

test<- plant_pairs %>%
  count(year, site, web)


# Run the loop for just this subset
datalist_overlap_test <- vector("list", length = nrow(plant_pairs_test))

for (i in 1:nrow(plant_pairs_test)) {
  tryCatch({
    dat <- inter_synchrony(i, plant_pairs_test, pheno_distributions)
    if (!is.null(dat)) datalist_overlap_test[[i]] <- dat
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Error in pair ", i, ": ", e$message)
    NULL
  })
}

# Combine results
plant_plant_overlap_test <- rbindlist(datalist_overlap_test, fill = TRUE)

# Inspect
summary(plant_plant_overlap_test)

#####VISUALIZATION OF OVERLAP

# pick one pair to illustrate
pick <- plant_plant_overlap_test[2, ]
sp1 <- pick$species.x
sp2 <- pick$species.y

# the two density curves for THAT pair, in THAT year/site/web
curves <- pheno_distributions %>%
  filter(year == pick$year, site == pick$site, web == pick$web,
         species %in% c(sp1, sp2)) %>%
  select(DOY, species, abund)

ov <- curves %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = species, values_from = abund) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(min_d = pmin(.data[[sp1]], .data[[sp2]]))

delta <- sfsmisc::integrate.xy(ov$DOY, ov$min_d)   # == pick$overlap

# actual observation dates: months where this pair flowered, mapped to DOY
month_to_doy <- c(`3`=80, `4`=110, `5`=140, `6`=170, `7`=200,
                  `8`=230, `9`=260, `10`=290)

obs <- phen_flower_long %>%
  filter(year == pick$year, site == pick$site, web == pick$web,
         species %in% c(sp1, sp2), flospec_count > 0) %>%
  mutate(DOY = month_to_doy[as.character(month)],
         DOY_stag = DOY + ifelse(species == sp1, -4, 4))

ggplot(curves, aes(DOY, abund, linetype = species, group = species)) +
  geom_area(data = ov, aes(DOY, min_d), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            fill = "grey60", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, color = "black") +
  geom_rug(data = obs, aes(x = DOY_stag), inherit.aes = FALSE,
           sides = "b", linewidth = 0.8, color = "black") +
  annotate("text", x = 200, y = max(curves$abund) * 0.95, hjust = 0,
           fontface = "bold",
           label = paste0("Overlap (\u0394) = ", round(delta, 3))) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames(c("solid", "dashed"), c(sp1, sp2))) +
  labs(x = "Day of Year", y = "Flowering Density") +
  ms_theme

```

```{r run_overlap_parallel}
library(data.table)
library(future)
library(furrr)

n <- nrow(plant_pairs)
years <- plant_pairs$year
sites <- plant_pairs$site
webs <- plant_pairs$web
species_x <- plant_pairs$species.x
species_y <- plant_pairs$species.y

plan(multisession, workers = parallel::detectCores() - 1)

# Run overlap calculation in parallel, returning just a single numeric value per pair
overlaps <- future_map_dbl(1:n, function(i) {
  tryCatch({
    # Run inter_synchrony and extract only the 'overlap' column
    inter_synchrony(i, plant_pairs, pheno_distributions)$overlap
  }, error = function(e) NA_real_)
}, .progress = TRUE)

plan(sequential)

# Combine into a clean data.table
plant_plant_overlap <- data.table(
  year = plant_pairs$year,
  site = plant_pairs$site,
  web = plant_pairs$web,
  species.x = plant_pairs$species.x,
  species.y = plant_pairs$species.y,
  overlap = overlaps
)

str(plant_plant_overlap)
summary(plant_plant_overlap$overlap)

# Save output
write.csv(plant_plant_overlap, "data/plant_plant_overlapthru2024.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
Now we have generated a csv containing the co-flowering overlap values of each species pair in a given year/site/web.
We will use this data for all downstream analyses.

### richness rarefaction of co-flowering overlap
Is mean overlap higher simply because more species (higher richness) are sampled? For each transect-year community we draw random subsets of increasing richness from the species present and average their pairwise overlaps (resampled many times), then plot richness vs mean overlap colored by that year's PDO. Conceptually a rarefaction: holds the number of species sampled constant to ask whether richness still shifts overlap. (slow resampling loop; set eval=TRUE to run)
```{r richness_rarefaction_overlap}
ov <- read.csv("data/plant_plant_overlapthru2024.csv")
ov <- overlap %>%
  filter(!site %in% c("J", "P", "JSAV"))

ov$site <- as.factor(ov$site)
ov$species.x <- as.factor(ov$species.x)
ov$species.y <- as.factor(ov$species.y)


# annual PDO
pdo_raw <- read.csv("data/pdo.timeseries.ersstv5.csv")
pdo_yr  <- aggregate(pdo_raw[[3]], list(year = pdo_raw$year), mean, na.rm = TRUE)
names(pdo_yr) <- c("year", "PDO")

communities <- unique(ov[, c("year","site","web")])
rows <- list()
for (i in 1:nrow(communities)) {
  yr <- communities$year[i]; st <- communities$site[i]; wb <- communities$web[i]
  sub <- ov[ov$year == yr & ov$site == st & ov$web == wb, ]
  sp  <- unique(c(sub$species.x, sub$species.y))
  if (length(sp) < 3) next
  for (S in 2:length(sp)) {
    for (r in 1:50) {
      pick <- sample(sp, S)
      pr   <- sub[sub$species.x %in% pick & sub$species.y %in% pick, ]
      if (nrow(pr) == 0) next
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- 
        data.frame(year = yr, site = st, web = wb,
        richness = S,
        mean_overlap = mean(pr$overlap, na.rm = TRUE))
    }
  }
}
rare <- do.call(rbind, rows)
rare <- dplyr::left_join(rare, pdo_yr, by = "year")

# richness (x) vs resampled mean overlap (y); one smoothed line per year,color is PDO
rarefaction_plot <- ggplot(rare, aes(x = richness, y = mean_overlap, color = PDO, group = year)) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, method = "loess", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "PDO") +
  labs(x = "Species richness (resampled)", y = "Mean co-flowering overlap") +
  ms_theme
rarefaction_plot
ggsave("figures/richness_rarefaction_overlap.png", rarefaction_plot, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```
